title: Statistics Office publishes latest March inflation data
text:
The Central Statistical Office (GUS) released its preliminary inflation report for March today. According to the official data, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) stood at 2.5% year-over-year. This figure represents a slight deceleration compared to the previous months of the year.

The primary drivers of the current inflation rate remain the services sector and food prices, which saw moderate increases. On the other hand, energy and fuel prices have stabilized, providing some relief to the overall index. Market analysts noted that the published data is fully aligned with earlier economic forecasts.

In a statement, the head of the statistical office emphasized that macroeconomic indicators suggest a stabilization of the market. The next comprehensive report, including a detailed breakdown of individual product categories, is scheduled for publication early next month.
author: Anna Nowak
label: High
justification: Neutral and professional tone, citation of an official institution (GUS), known author, multi-paragraph structured text, lack of emotional phrasing.

title: SHOCK! The government is HIDING the truth about 6G!!!
text:

Because they don't want you to see what they are doing to our neighborhoods!

Don't let them fool you any longer. Share this article with everyone you know before they take this website down and block us forever! The truth will prevail!!!

label: Low
justification: Excessive punctuation (!!!), all-caps words (SHOCK, HIDING, Big Tech), anonymous author, conspiracy theory narrative, call to action for rapid sharing, lack of verifiable sources or evidence.

title: This one simple trick will make you lose 10 kg in a week
text:
Millions of people struggle with weight loss every day, spending thousands on expensive gym memberships and strict diets that never work. But recently, doctors have been absolutely furious with one woman who discovered a shocking secret.

She managed to lose over 10 kilograms in just seven days without lifting a single weight or starving herself. Her method makes stubborn belly fat disappear in the blink of an eye, and the fitness industry is trying to hide it because they are losing money.

The secret is surprisingly simple. All you have to do is drink a warm glass of water mixed with a common kitchen ingredient every single morning before breakfast. Read on to find out what this miracle ingredient is and how you can start today!
author: Editorial Team
label: Medium
justification: Classic clickbait strategy. Manipulative language ('doctors are furious'), promises of unrealistic medical/biological results, withholding the main information until the end (curiosity gap) to farm clicks. Low factual value.

title: New research on the effectiveness of gene therapy in oncology
text:
A groundbreaking study published yesterday in the prestigious scientific journal 'Nature' offers new hope for cancer patients worldwide. A team of international researchers has presented the results of phase II clinical trials evaluating a novel viral vector designed for targeted gene therapy.

The clinical trial focused on patients diagnosed with advanced, treatment-resistant melanoma. According to the published data, partial remission of tumors was observed in approximately 30% of the participants. Furthermore, the therapy demonstrated a manageable safety profile, with fewer severe side effects than traditional chemotherapy.

Despite the promising results, the authors of the study urge caution. They emphasize that the method is still in its early stages and requires larger, multi-center phase III trials to fully confirm its long-term efficacy and safety before it can be approved for general medical use.
author: Prof. Peter Smith
label: High
justification: Author with a verifiable academic title, direct reference to a reputable scientific journal ('Nature'), cautious and balanced scientific language ('requires further testing'), includes specific statistics and trial phases.

title: Will the new tax ruin families? Experts sound the alarm
text:
The Ministry of Finance announced a new legislative proposal yesterday aimed at introducing an environmental fee on major industrial producers. While the government officially claims that the changes will only impact large corporations and encourage green transitions, independent analysts are deeply skeptical.

A new report by the Free Market Institute suggests that the financial burden will ultimately be shifted down to the consumer level. Experts warn that this could lead to a drastic inflation of utility bills, potentially raising household electricity prices by up to 15% by the end of the year.

Opposition leaders have already slammed the proposal, calling it an indirect tax on ordinary citizens during a time of economic uncertainty. As the debate heats up in parliament, many families are left wondering how they will manage these projected increases in their cost of living.
author: Thomas Taylor
label: Medium
justification: The text is based on a real event (a proposed fee) and cites actual viewpoints, but uses highly sensationalized and emotional language in the headline ('ruin', 'sound the alarm') to provoke anxiety. Testing this helps evaluate how a model distinguishes between objective news and biased commentary.
